name: Pashtun nationalism
summary: Pashtun nationalism holds that the Pashtuns are a distinct people with their own language, culture and homeland, divided by the colonial Durand Line and other borders. Its main current, from the Khudai Khidmatgars through the Awami National Party to the Pashtun Tahafuz Movement, seeks Pashtun unity, autonomy and rights by non-violent means, while an Afghan state strand pressed for a Greater Pashtunistan.
scope: The Khudai Khidmatgar tradition of Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1929-1947) and its heirs, the Awami National Party (2018 programme) and the Pashtun Tahafuz Movement, with the Afghan state claim to Pashtunistan recorded as a documented split where it differs. It excludes Taliban Islamism and Pakistani or Afghan state nationalism that is not Pashtun-nationalist. The ANP programme answers only where nothing from the other strands contradicts it.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The ANP programme commits to improved access to quality health services for all citizens, 6 percent of GDP for health and primary care, through a mix of insurance, public-private partnership and public provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The ANP programme promises to review the minimum wage regularly against living costs and to raise it from the current level to Rs 25,000.

unions-good.rationale: The ANP programme says trade unions are critical to protecting labour rights and living standards and promises to amend laws that restrict them.

decide-locally.rationale: The ANP programme calls for devolution of powers from the federal level to the provinces and districts and treats local government as an important democratic tier.

rehabilitation.rationale: The ANP programme plans correctional centres with education, sports and library provision and juvenile centres focused on education and rehabilitation.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The ANP programme proposes replacing security check posts with enhanced intelligence and state-of-the-art surveillance to counter terrorism.

more-religion-public.rationale: The ANP programme aims at a secular state and blames the misuse of religion in politics for violent conflict, so it does not seek a larger public role for religion.

separate-church-state.rationale: The ANP programme aims for a secular democratic state, but the 1947 Bannu demand for a Pashtun state spoke of a constitution on an Islamic concept of democracy, so the tradition is not uniform.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The 1947 Khudai Khidmatgar demand drew on Pashtun cultural values and an Islamic concept of democracy, whereas the ANP programme opposes parochial religious interpretation and seeks a secular state.

clerical-rule.rationale: The ANP programme seeks a secular democratic welfare state and opposes the misuse of religion in politics, which leaves no place for rule by senior religious scholars.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Khudai Khidmatgar oath commits members to seeking the will of God and to freedom of their religion, and the movement promoted love of Islam among Pashtuns.

religious-nation.rationale: The Khudai Khidmatgars admitted members of every religion and the ANP programme gives equal rights irrespective of religion, so the Pashtun nation is not defined by shared religion.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The movement revived Pashto language and literature and Pashtun cultural identity, and the ANP programme promises to preserve cultural heritage, while also opposing parochial customs.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: Ghaffar Khan sought to end blood-feuds and lavish customs, and the ANP programme opposes parochial customs and seeks to end child marriage, swara and vani.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Khudai Khidmatgar oath binds members to non-violence, the PTM and the ANP reject violence in all its forms; Afghan state backing of tribal militias is not the movement tradition.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Non-violence is the oath and defining principle of the Khudai Khidmatgars, and the ANP stands against violence in all its forms, which excludes targeting civilians.

war-builds-character.rationale: Ghaffar Khan said in 1939 that the movement had been condemning war and its horrors and resisted dragging the Pashtuns into war.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: Ghaffar Khan rejected the armed struggle of Haji Sahib of Turangzai against the Raj as ruinous and held the Khudai Khidmatgars to non-violence under British occupation.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: A strict non-violence pledge and Ghaffar Khan's rejection of armed struggle exclude an armed vanguard making revolution.

property-sabotage-justified.rationale: The oath binds members to non-violence, and the movement kept to it under flogging and firing.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Ghaffar Khan rejected armed jihad against the British and led a non-violent Muslim movement; the Pashtun tradition here is that of Khudai Khidmatgar non-violence.

direct-action.rationale: The Khudai Khidmatgars used civil disobedience, but the ANP contests elections and governs, and the PTM combines jalsas with courts and parliament.

civil-disobedience-accept-penalty.rationale: Khudai Khidmatgars pledged not to give security or apologise during the fight, and Ghaffar Khan and others served prison sentences rather than retreat.

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: The oath pledges to sacrifice wealth, comfort and self for the liberation of the country and to help the oppressed against the oppressor; hundreds died unarmed at Qissa Khwani.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The oath pledges to serve all human beings alike, and the ANP programme commits to equal rights and opportunities for all irrespective of gender, religion, race, class and creed.

women-suffrage.rationale: The ANP programme gives every citizen the right to hold any public office, seeks women's equal political participation and repeal of discriminatory laws; the Red Shirts mobilised women into public life.

reserved-seats-excluded-groups.rationale: The ANP programme reserves seats for non-Muslims, adds seats for religious minorities and sets a 33 percent minimum for women.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The ANP programme calls for implementing women's right to inheritance and ending customary discriminatory practices.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The ANP programme strengthens ministries and commissions on the status of women, and its provincial government set up a provincial commission.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Red Shirt Movement resisted purdah and worked for women's equal rights, and the ANP programme repeals discriminatory laws.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Pashtun nationalists treat the Durand Line as dividing a shared Pashtun homeland, and the movement promoted Pashtun unity through Pashto language and culture.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Khudai Khidmatgars sought liberation and in 1947 demanded a Pashtun state option, Afghan governments pressed for Pashtunistan, while the ANP and PTM work within Pakistan's federation.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The 1947 Bannu meeting demanded an autonomous Pashtun state and the ANP programme commits to provincial autonomy and reorganising units on historic, cultural and linguistic lines.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The ANP programme pledges to unite the Pakhtun within Pakistan by removing colonial divisions, merged FATA with Pakhtunkhwa and aims to bring Pakhtun districts of Balochistan in too.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Afghan governments pressed for a Greater Pashtunistan across the Durand Line, while the ANP programme seeks unity only within Pakistan and PTM is said to be wrongly accused of seeking Afghan unification.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Pashtun nationalists and Afghan governments argued the Durand agreement was signed under duress and without consulting Pashtuns, but the ANP programme works within Pakistan's existing borders.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Afghan governments never recognised the Durand Line while the ANP programme operates inside the border Pakistan inherited.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Daoud-era Afghanistan claimed Pashtun areas of Pakistan, whereas the ANP programme seeks relations on sovereign equality and non-interference.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Ghaffar Khan demanded that the 1947 referendum offer a Pashtunistan option, and nationalists argue Pashtuns were never given a plebiscite on the Durand Line, though the Khudai Khidmatgars boycotted the vote held.

democracy-best.rationale: The ANP programme is dedicated to promoting democracy and freedom and strengthening the democratic process.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The ANP programme vows to resist any attempt to roll back the 18th Amendment or federal encroachment on devolved subjects.

regional-resource-ownership.rationale: The ANP programme demands provincial rights over their own resources, including oil, gas, water and power, under the 18th Amendment.

minority-language-support.rationale: The ANP programme promotes primary education in the mother tongue and unrestricted development of the languages of the provinces.

single-official-language.rationale: The ANP programme backs mother-tongue schooling and the languages of the provinces alongside Urdu and English.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: PTM leaders sought a truth and reconciliation commission to hold the military and officials accountable for abuses.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Ending extra-judicial killings is one of the PTM's six goals, and the ANP programme upholds rule of law and access to justice.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: PTM demands an end to enforced disappearances and fair trials for the detained, and the ANP programme upholds rule of law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The ANP programme states commitment to freedom of association and expression and to the right to information in letter and spirit.

party-controls-media.rationale: The ANP programme commits to freedom of expression and association, which excludes government control of the media.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The ANP programme is committed to freedom of association, democratic process and pluralism, and the movement itself suffered ban and repression.

one-party-rule.rationale: The ANP programme commits to the democratic and political process and pluralism, which excludes rule by a single ideological party.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The ANP programme states that it opposes any interference in politics by civil and military bureaucracy and that institutions must stay within constitutional limits.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The ANP programme seeks political solutions rather than force and a foreign policy rooted in non-violence, peace and mutual respect.

arms-reduction.rationale: The ANP programme supports international moves for arms reduction and abolition of nuclear weapons on a universal, non-discriminatory basis.

multipolar-world.rationale: The ANP programme promotes a multipolar world which would avoid universal domination by one or two major powers.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The ANP programme calls for an independent foreign policy that avoids regional great games and warns against being a tool of powerful countries.

non-intervention.rationale: The ANP programme conducts relations with Afghanistan and neighbours on sovereign equality and non-interference in internal affairs.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Daoud-era Kabul backed tribal militias across the border, while the ANP and PTM oppose proxy militancy and criticise the army's support for the Taliban.

close-ties-china.rationale: The ANP programme says close relations with China will be maintained and developed, while normalising relations with the United States on mutual interest.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The ANP programme bases foreign relations on sovereign equality and rejects abject surrender to great powers.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The ANP programme bases foreign relations on sovereign equality and non-interference in internal affairs.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Khudai Khidmatgars fought British imperial rule and the ANP programme honours the struggle to free South Asia from foreign domination.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The movement opposed colonial domination of the Pashtuns and of South Asia as exploitation.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The ANP preamble names the weak, disadvantaged and dispossessed as those whose aspirations the party serves and pledges to eradicate poverty.

cut-welfare.rationale: The ANP programme aims to transform the state into a secular, democratic welfare state with social security and old-age benefits.

state-harmful.rationale: The ANP programme builds on state institutions, welfare and the rule of law, and gives the state the task of offering peace and security.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The ANP programme calls for a welfare state providing health, education and social security.

total-state.rationale: The ANP programme commits to freedom of association, expression and pluralism, which excludes a state directing every area of life.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The ANP is itself a party committed to the democratic and political process.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The ANP programme weighs health insurance, public-private partnership and support to the private health sector alongside public provision.

farm-price-support.rationale: The ANP programme announces support prices giving small growers a minimum guaranteed income and extends agricultural credit to small farmers.

limit-population.rationale: The ANP programme doubles per capita public spending on population planning and expands birth-spacing services.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The ANP programme commits to equal rights irrespective of race and repeal of discriminatory laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: The ANP programme gives every citizen equal political rights and the right to hold any public office irrespective of race.

population-transfer.rationale: The oath pledges to serve all human beings alike and the ANP programme guarantees security and equal rights to ethnic minorities.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: Serving all human beings alike and equal rights for all nationalities and groups, as the oath and ANP programme state, exclude expelling ethnic groups.

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: Helping the oppressed against the oppressor, as the oath pledges, and equal rights for all nationalities, as the ANP programme states, exclude removing peoples from their lands.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The ANP programme promises to expand space for creative cultural expression and to support artists and writers.

military-organisation-revolutionary-part.rationale: The Khudai Khidmatgars were organised, drilled and ranked in military fashion, though bound to non-violence.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Members swore to obey every lawful order of their officers and not to join any rival party, and the leaders stressed discipline.
